```{r load-packages, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)
```

## Introduction

Using the NYTimes API, I explore which books are listed as the top 10 best sellers in the middle grade hardback category. 


## API Request
First I make the request. This requires access to the "Books" API. My endpoint is the list of top middle grade hardcover books. I have my API key saved in my R environment file, *not* hardcoded into my quarto file or uploaded to github.
```{r api-request}
nyt_key <- Sys.getenv("NYT_API_KEY")
mg_books_url <- "https://api.nytimes.com/svc/books/v3/lists/current/childrens-middle-grade-hardcover.json"
response <- GET(mg_books_url, query = list(`api-key` = nyt_key))
```

## Convert to Data Frame
Once we have the response to our API query, we can parse the JSON request and convert it to data frame. 
```{r convert-to-df}
# Parse the JSON
json_text <- content(response, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8")
parsed_data <- fromJSON(json_text, flatten = TRUE)

# Extract into a data frame
mgbooks_df <- parsed_data$results$books

```

## Tidy Data Frame
Finally I tidy the data frame by selecting only relevant, non-empty columns. A preview of the first 10 entries in that list is displayed:
```{r tidy-df}
clean_mgbooks <- mgbooks_df %>%
  select(
    rank,
    title,
    author,
    publisher,
    description,
    weeks_on_list,
    primary_isbn13,
    age_group
  )

# Display the top 5 middle grade best sellers
head(clean_mgbooks %>% select(rank,title, author), n=10)
```
